transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I guess what really pushed me to come in is work. I can’t shake this feeling that people there, and even some of the vendors, are tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. My supervisor has shown me the reports and says they don’t prove that, but it still feels like it’s happening.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other recreational drugs recently?
I don’t really have anything specific to say there. I mean, I’m not sure what counts as “recently,” but I haven’t noticed anything like that being a big part of what’s going on.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any periods where your mood felt unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep?

Yeah… I do get stretches like that. It’s like I feel suddenly really up, like the whole city is kind of opening up for me and I can move faster than everybody else. And then if someone questions a purchase order or tells me to slow down, I snap at them way harder than I mean to.

During times when you're not feeling that surge of energy or irritability—when your mood feels more normal—do you still find yourself believing that people at work are tracking your purchases and messing with the numbers?

Yeah. Even when I’m calmer and sleeping more normal, it doesn’t really go away. There was a stretch like that for a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling all sped up or like I was running the whole market, but I still believed people were tracking my buys and messing with the numbers. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom sometimes.

Thinking back over the entire time you've had these beliefs and heard that voice, would you say the manic or energized periods have been present for most of that time, or have there been long stretches—weeks or months—where you had the beliefs and voice but no mood changes at all?

Most of the time, I think those wired or irritable periods have been there. Like since this started, I’ve usually been overworking, feeling too confident, hard to slow down, that kind of thing. There have been calmer stretches in between, but they’ve felt shorter, not like months and months where it was only the beliefs and the voice with no mood change.
During that stretch when you felt calmer and weren't experiencing the high energy or irritability, but still had the beliefs and the voice, about how many days or weeks did that stretch last?

It was a few weeks, I think. I wasn’t feeling all sped up then, and I was sleeping more normal, but I still thought people were tracking my buys, and I still heard the voice in the stockroom sometimes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports concurrent, overlapping manic symptoms (elevated/expansive mood, grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, increased energy, irritability) and psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions about coworkers/vendors tracking purchases and sabotaging launch numbers, auditory hallucinations of a voice in the stockroom). Critically, the delusions and hallucinations persisted during a distinct multi-week period when mood/energy symptoms were absent, confirming psychosis occurs independent of mood episodes (ruling out mood disorder with psychotic features). However, this psychosis-only stretch was only a few weeks, while manic/irritable mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total illness duration, ruling out primary psychotic disorder (schizophrenia) where mood episodes would be brief relative to the psychotic illness. No substance use was reported that could account for symptoms. This pattern—concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms with mood episodes present for a majority of the illness course, plus at least 2 weeks of psychosis without mood symptoms—meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type.
